We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 5 reactions, using templates in order: ['29646', '1914389', '1914390', '149040', '1914391'].

We have applied 29646 to target, got three possible precursors (list of three). Need to choose one that can be further processed with next template 1914389, then 1914390, then 149040, then 1914391.

We need to construct a tree JSON with each reaction node having children precursors (mol nodes). For each step, we need to apply the template to the product (starting from target) to get precursors, then apply next template to each precursor? Usually retrosynthesis: each reaction splits a molecule into precursors. So we need a linear route of 5 steps: target -> after template 29646 gives precursor A (maybe one). Then apply 1914389 to that precursor to get B, etc.

We need to find a chain where each template matches.

From first apply 29646 gave three possible precursors:

Result string: "(('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C',), ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO',), ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C',))"

So three options: 1) with silyl protecting groups on both CO and acid; 2) with silyl on acid only? Actually second has no silyl on CO? It ends with CO (no silyl). Third is simpler: no silyl, just core.

We need to apply template 1914389 next. We attempted applying to some forms earlier; we succeeded on the second (with CO but no silyl?) Actually we applied 1914389 to "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO" and got precursors: ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO', 'CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC').

So that works: template 1914389 applied to that molecule (which is the second precursor from 29646? Actually second had no silyl on CO but had silyl on acid? Wait second string: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO". That still has silyl on acid. The one we succeeded on had no silyl on acid: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO". So we need to get that as precursor from 29646. The third option is "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C". That's different.

Thus maybe we need to choose a different path: maybe apply 29646 to get the third precursor, then apply 1914389 to that? Let's test applying 1914389 to third precursor.
